analyticalQuestion: Can the complete product-affine charge-weight family materially improve the R0.53 witness in the degree-80 reduced edge model, and can the entire noncompact parameter family be enclosed without a parameter grid?
supportedClaim: For the exact degree-80 reduced canonical edge generating system, the complete compactified product-affine family satisfies 0.382628602237879637 < r_prod^opt < 0.382629. Relative to the complete R0.52 affine-family upper bound, its gain is strictly between 10.7948905 and 11.8344532 ppm. Complete optimization can improve the R0.53 witness by a factor smaller than 1.0000010395514554756.

chartContract.family: exact compactified invariant domain, formal gain enclosure, and complete dyadic cover map

two formal exact gain endpoints and one separately classified 100-digit diagnostic point

chartContract.takeaway: The entire product-affine family is globally enclosed inside a 3.97762120363e-7 radius interval. Its possible improvement above the fixed R0.53 witness is less than about 1.0396 ppm, so increasing this weight polynomial degree fails the predeclared 1e-4 continuation threshold.
chartContract.dataSufficiency: The boundary samples and 64 optimizer starts are not proof data. The theorem uses the pinned exact invariant reduction, exact character-tail theorems, and the complete 14-leaf GMP tensor-Bernstein certificate.
